In this appeal, the petitioner apart from seeking enhancement, is also questioning the liability fastened against the owner of the bus and the owner of the bus is also challenging the liability fastened against him.
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 16.11.2011 at 8.00 p.m., while the petitioner was traveling in a Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-16/A-9698, at Upparahally bus stop the petitioner was about to get down from the said bus, but the driver of the bus moved it negligently, due to which he fell down from the bus and the back wheel of the bus ran over on his right foot injuring him.

After taking treatment at Government Hospital, Hiriyur, District Hospital Chitradurga and C.G.Hospital Davanagere from 17.11.2011 to 15.01.2012, the NC: 2024:KHC:38057 petitioner has approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation.

3.1 Before the Tribunal, the owner of the bus was placed exparte, the insurance company alone has contested the claim that the driver of the bus one Abuthurab Ali was subsequently brought in for the reason of Rafeeq was not holding D.L.

The Tribunal, after taking the evidence and hearing both the parties, allowed the claim petition granting compensation of Rs.2,70,600/- with interest at 7.5% p.a.
and directed the owner of the vehicle to pay compensation and dismissed the claim petition against the insurance company.
Assailing the same, both the petitioner as well as the owner of the bus are before this Court on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Shri N.R.Range Gowda, learned counsel for the petitioner, Shri B.M.Siddappa, learned counsel for the owner of the bus NC: 2024:KHC:38057 and Shri Janardhan Reddy, learned counsel for the insurance company.
5.
It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is an innocent-illiterate person suffered injuries in the accident.
Even after 13 years of the accident he is unable to receive any compensation.

The averments made in the complaint that one Rafeeq was the driver of the bus was not the statement of the petitioner, the narration made in the complaint is in the Police language and the Police have taken the LTM of the petitioner in order to register FIR.

During the course of investigation, it is recorded that the name of the driver was Abuthurab Ali @
Rafeeq, accordingly charge sheet was filed.
Driver was holding effective D.L. to drive the bus, the policy of insurance was in force, the insurance company is liable to indemnify the owner of the bus.

The compensation awarded is on the lower side, the petitioner being a coolie lost his earning capacity and the compensation NC: 2024:KHC:38057 awarded is disproportionate to the nature of injuries and sought for enhancement of compensation.
6.
Learned counsel for the owner of the bus has contended that unfortunately the owner was placed exparte before the Tribunal.
The driver of the bus was Rafeeq, he has been called in his sir name as 'Rafeeq' and the documentary name is 'Abuthurab Ali'.

This has been informed to the Police,
accordingly the Police have filed the charge sheet in the name of Abuthurab Ali @ Rafeeq and both the persons are one and the same.
The insurance company has not let any evidence to prove that Rafeeq and Abuthurab Ali are different persons.
There is no investigation report available to the insurance company.
In the absence of any evidence, the Tribunal has rightly accepted that Abuthurab Ali @ Rafeeq was the same person.
The Tribunal has not accepted the said explanation and has erroneously fastened liability against the owner.

There is valid insurance as well as the policy is in force and NC: 2024:KHC:38057 the risk of the owner is covered by the policy, insurance company on irrelevant grounds tried to avoiding its liability and sought for fastening of the liability on the insurance company.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurance company has contended that in the objection statement there is a specific defense taken that the name of the driver of the bus was Rafeeq.

The FIR came to be registered after recording the statement of the injured in the Hospital after 27 days of the accident, so by that time who was the driver of the bus was very well known to the complainant as well as the Police.
The Abuthurab Ali is not the Rafeeq.
No evidence is placed on record that Rafeeq was also called as Abuthurab Ali by anywhere either in the form of documentary evidence or in the form of oral evidence.

The Tribunal is right in accepting that Rafeeq is different and Abuthurab Ali is different and has rightly fastened the liability against the owner to pay NC:
2024:KHC:38057 the compensation.

It is further contended that the compensation awarded is proportionate to the nature of injuries, avocation of the petitioner and it is not a case for enhancement.
8.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both parties and perused the records.

9. Materials on record goes to show that the accident took place on 16.11.2011 at 8.00 p.m. while the petitioner was de-boarding the bus, it was moved abruptly pulling down the petitioner to the ground and back wheel of the bus ran over on the right foot of the petitioner, made him to suffer injuries under hospitalization for a period of 59 days.
The Police have visited the Hospital, recorded the statement of the petitioner and thereafter set the law into motion by filing FIR against one Rafeeq.
In the charge sheet, the name of Abuthurab Ali is forthcoming and his name is referred as Abuthurab Ali @ rafeeq.

Before the NC: 2024:KHC:38057 Tribunal, there is no evidence let in either by the petitioner, owner or the insurance company that Rafeeq is different and Abuthurab Ali is different or Rafeeq was also called as Abuthurab Ali.

sentences.text: On perusal of Ex.P1-complaint, it is pertinent to note that it is not the statement of the petitioner, it is completely written in the Police language.

The recitals clearly goes to show that the petitioner had never stated that Rafeeq was the driver of the bus, but the statement made in Ex.P1 shows that the petitioner came to know that the driver of the bus was one Rafeeq.
After investigation, the charge sheet was filed against the driver of the bus as Abuthurab Ali @ Rafeeq.
Unfortunately, the owner of the bus was placed exparte, it is his duty to appear before the Tribunal and assist for effective disposal of the claim petition.
11. The notice issued by the Investigating Officer under Section 133 of the Motor Vehicles Act is also not - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:38057 produced before the Tribunal.
The person who recorded the statement of the petitioner and the person who filed the charge sheet were also not examined.

The co-passengers of the bus at the time of accident would be the better persons to speak of who was the driver of the bus whether it was Rafeeq or Abuthurab Ali, or whether Rafeeq was also called as Abuthurab Ali.
Under such circumstances, the Tribunal is completely handicapped in determining who was the actual driver of the bus at the time of accident.
Unless the identity of driver is established, it is very difficult to accept that Abuthurab Ali was also called as Rafeeq.
To appreciate the D.L. produced today by the learned counsel for the petitioner.

The extract of D.L did not refer Abuthurab Ali as @ Rafeeq.
12.
Instead of deciding the appeal on merits, it is going to affect on the liability on the part of the owner of the bus and also it would affect the petitioner in getting higher compensation.
The petitioner having - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:38057 sustained injuries must be awarded with just compensation.
Mere remanding the matter will not suffice.
The statutory deposit of Rs.25,000/- is already made by the owner.
Apart from the same, as per the order of this Court, a sum of Rs.1,51,000/- has been deposited before this Court.

In addition to that, the owner must be directed to deposit another sum of Rs.75,000/- before the Tribunal and let the matter be go before the Tribunal for reassessment of compensation as well as the determination of the liability on the part of the insurance company to indemnify the owner.
The amount that will be deposited shall be kept in FD and whoever succeeds is entitled to receive said compensation.
Hence, it is a fit case for remand.
In view of the remand is inevitable, it is not a case for re-determination of compensation.

13. Accordingly, the appeal filed by the petitioner has become infructuous and the appeal filed by the - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:38057 owner of the bus merits consideration, in the result, the following:
